source.section: Schedule 1S lines 3, 4 and 27, the Worksheet for Pension Income Deduction lines P1-P10 and the Worksheet for Phaseout of Non-Military Pension Income Deduction lines 1-5 (Schedule 1S PDF p.2); booklet Schedule 1S line 3 (PDF p.7) and line 4 (PDF p.8); Form 1040ME lines 14-20; line 17 chart and Worksheet for Standard / Itemized Deductions lines 1-8 (booklet PDF p.5); line 18 (PDF p.5); 2025 Tax Rate Schedules (PDF p.13). Record cite: pension_income_deduction, PDF page 8, 36 M.R.S. 5122(2)(M-2); income_test width 100,000 (50,000 married filing separately) and share to four decimals from the phaseout worksheet lines 4 and 5 (Schedule 1S PDF p.2)

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 115,011.00 + IRA distribution (person 0) 30,000.00 = 145,011.00. Federal taxable income = 145,011.00 - 15,750.00 standard deduction - 1 x 1,600.00 for 65 or older = 127,661.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form 1040ME, married filing separately: line 14 federal AGI 145,011.00. Schedule 1A line 1 (PDF p.7) other-state municipal bond interest 0.00; Schedule 1A total = line 15a 0.00. Schedule 1S line 3 (PDF p.7) taxable Social Security 0.00 + railroad retirement 0.00 = 0.00. Worksheet for Phaseout of Non-Military Pension Income Deduction (Schedule 1S PDF p.2): line 1 federal AGI 145,011.00; line 2 125,000.00; line 3 20,011.00; line 4 50,000.00; line 5 = 20,011.00 / 50,000.00 = 0.40022, entered to four decimals as 0.4002. Pension Income Deduction Worksheet (taxpayer column, person 0, age 67): P1 eligible non-military pension income 30,000.00; P2 48,216.00; P3 Social Security and railroad benefits received 0.00; P4 = 48,216.00 - 0.00 = 48,216.00; P5 smaller of P1 and P4 = 30,000.00; P6 0.4002; P7 = 30,000.00 x 0.4002 = 12,006.00; P8 = 17,994.00; P9 military retirement pay 0.00; P10 = 17,994.00. Schedule 1S line 4 = P10 total 17,994.00 (non-military 17,994.00 + military 0.00). Schedule 1S line 27 total subtractions = 0.00 + 17,994.00 = line 15b 17,994.00. Line 16 Maine AGI = 145,011.00 + 0.00 - 17,994.00 = 127,017.00. Line 17 (person 0 born 1958-08-20 is 67 at December 31, 2025; 1 box(es)): Worksheet for Standard/Itemized Deductions (PDF p.5): line 1 127,017.00; line 2 100,000.00; line 3 27,017.00; line 4 75,000.00; line 5 = 0.360227..., entered to four decimals as 0.3602; line 6 chart amount 16,600.00; line 7 = 16,600.00 x 0.3602 = 5,979.32; line 8 = 10,620.68. Projection (share kept 1 - 0.3602 = 0.6398): base 15,000.00 x 0.6398 = 9,597.00 + additional 65-or-over 1 x 1,600.00 x 0.6398 = 1,023.68 = 10,620.68, the same. Line 17 = 10,620.68. Line 13 = 1; line 18 exemption = 1 x 5,150.00 = 5,150.00 (Maine AGI not over 200,050.00). Line 19 taxable income = 127,017.00 - 10,620.68 - 5,150.00 = 111,246.32. Line 20 tax from the rate schedule (PDF p.13): 5.8% x (26,800.00 - 0.00) = 1,554.40 + 6.75% x (63,450.00 - 26,800.00) = 2,473.875 + 7.15% x (111,246.32 - 63,450.00) = 3,417.43688 = 7,445.71188, 7,445.71 to the cent. The printed schedule (PDF p.13) with its whole-dollar constant 4,028.00 gives 7,445.44; expected keeps the bracket tax computed in full. Line 23 nonrefundable credits 0.00; line 24 Maine income tax 7,445.71. Married filing separately: phaseout width 50,000 (worksheet line 4); line 13 is 1 (no spouse exemption claimed) and only the filer's own 65-or-over box counts (chart 16,600).
accepted_approximations: Tax is computed from the rate schedules as numbers. The booklet's table taxes 100-dollar rows and the printed schedule constants are rounded to dollars.
